title: Climb
subtitle: Costs 1 extra foot per foot
description: Each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot of movement while climbing.

bullets.content: If you have a Climb Speed, you ignore this extra cost. The DM might require a Strength (Athletics) check if the climb is difficult.

title: Crawl
subtitle: Costs 1 extra foot per foot
description: Each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot of movement while crawling.

bullets.content: Crawling is the primary way to move while you are in the Prone condition.

title: Difficult Terrain
subtitle: Costs 1 extra foot per foot
description: Moving in difficult terrain costs 1 extra foot for every foot of movement.

bullets.content: This extra cost isn't cumulative; a space is either difficult terrain or it isn't.

title: Drop Prone
subtitle: Cost: 0 feet of movement
description: You can drop prone without using any of your speed. This subjects you to the Prone condition.

bullets.content: To move while prone, you must crawl or use magic such as teleportation.

title: Flying
subtitle: Move through the air
description: If you have a fly speed, you can move through the air. You fall if you are Incapacitated, Prone, or your fly speed is reduced to 0.

bullets.content: A creature with the Hover trait can remain aloft even under these circumstances.

title: Grapple Move
subtitle: Costs 1 extra foot per foot
description: If you move while grappling another creature, every foot of movement costs 1 extra foot.

bullets.content: This extra cost is ignored if the grappled creature is Tiny or you are two or more sizes larger than it.

title: High Jump
subtitle: Leap vertically
description: You leap into the air a number of feet equal to 3 + your Strength modifier if you move at least 10 feet on foot immediately before the jump.

bullets.content: A standing high jump is half that distance. You can extend your arms half your height above yourself during the jump.

title: Improvise
subtitle: Perform any other movement
description: You can attempt any other movement you can imagine. The DM determines if it is possible and what might be required.

bullets.content: This allows for creative stunts like swinging on a chandelier or sliding down a staircase.

title: Long Jump
subtitle: Leap horizontally
description: You cover a number of feet up to your Strength score if you move at least 10 feet on foot immediately before the jump.

bullets.content: A standing long jump is half that distance. If you land in difficult terrain, you must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or be knocked Prone.

title: Move
subtitle: Use up to your Speed
description: On your turn, you can move a distance up to your Speed. This can be broken up before, after, and between your actions.

bullets.content: The rules for movement are as follows:

items: You can move through the space of an ally, an Incapacitated creature, a Tiny creature, or a creature that is two sizes larger or smaller than you.
Another creature's space is difficult terrain for you unless that creature is Tiny or your ally.
You can't willingly end your move in a space occupied by another creature.

bullets.content: Your movement can be broken up by actions and bonus actions.

title: Stand Up
subtitle: Cost: Half your speed
description: Standing up from the Prone condition costs an amount of movement equal to half of your Speed.

bullets.content: You can't stand up if you don't have enough movement left or if your speed is 0.

title: Swim
subtitle: Costs 1 extra foot per foot
description: Each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot of movement while swimming.

bullets.content: If you have a Swim Speed, you ignore this extra cost. The DM might require a Strength (Athletics) check if you are swimming in rough waters.

title: Travel Pace
subtitle: Movement over long distances
description: When traveling for an hour or more, you can move at a Fast, Normal, or Slow pace.

bullets.content: While traveling, your party should establish a marching order. The travel pace determines the distance covered:
A Fast pace imposes Disadvantage on certain checks, while a Slow pace grants Advantage on others.
